chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarquqi, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the ornamented sword for cash, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about selling it on credit, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the cash is equal to what is in its silver, then there is no problem with it, or let him give the foodstuff (as barter).'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling an ornamented sword on credit according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of selling an ornamented sword, distinguishing between cash and credit transactions by anchoring the latter to the intrinsic silver value (or foodstuff) to avoid riba (usury). This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of treating ornamental items as commodities with measurable intrinsic value rather than unique collectibles, ensuring fairness in deferred payment exchanges.
